check.disclaimer: This checklist is a guide, not legal advice. Have a lawyer confirm every step.

seller.title: Confirm who the seller is
seller.detail: Ask for the seller's national ID and check that the name matches the owner on the deed. If someone else is selling for them, ask to see a legal power of attorney.

deed.title: Read the deed carefully
deed.detail: Check the deed number, the owner's name, the size in perches and the date. Every detail should match what the seller tells you and what you see on the land.

boundaries.title: Compare the boundaries with the land
boundaries.detail: Walk the land. Check what lies on the north, east, south and west sides against the deed. Note the surroundings too: neighbours, canals, fields.

road.title: Confirm road access
road.detail: Check which side has the road and whether you have a legal right to use it. A plot with no proper access is hard to use or resell.

history.title: Trace the owners for about 15 years
history.detail: Ask for the chain of earlier deeds. Write down who owned the land, when it changed hands and how: sale, gift or inheritance. Gaps in the chain are a warning sign.

verify.title: Have the deed verified at the official registry
verify.detail: Usually through a lawyer, ask the official registry to confirm the deed is genuine and properly registered. Ask your lawyer which office does this.

forgery.title: Watch for signs of forgery
forgery.detail: Forged or altered deeds are a known risk. A lawyer should check signatures, stamps and numbers, and confirm the earlier deeds in the chain are real too.

legal.title: Check for legal problems
legal.detail: Look for court cases, disputes, mortgages or claims by other family members. Any of these can stop a sale or cost you the land.

lawyer.title: Get a lawyer's opinion before you pay
lawyer.detail: Ask a lawyer to review everything and give you a written opinion. Do not hand over money until this is done.
